description.value: Kekuli Cafe is an Indigenous-owned fast-casual cafe founded by Sharon Bond-Hogg of the Nooaitch First Nation, celebrating Indigenous culinary traditions through bannock-based sandwiches, tipi tacos, Mother Earth Bowls, and organic fair-trade espresso drinks. The menu draws on locally sourced ingredients and highlights traditional ingredients like venison, wild salmon, and saskatoon berries. It is part of a small BC franchise with locations in West Kelowna, Kelowna, Merritt, and Kamloops.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the West Kelowna location address as '307-3550 Carrington Road, West Kelowna, BC V4T2Z1', matching the OSM record exactly including unit 307. Takeout is confirmed by both OSM takeaway=yes and the FAQ page stating 'fast-casual restaurant offering dine-in and takeout options.' The menu page explicitly lists a 'Vegetarian Breakfast Bannock', confirming at least one vegetarian option; no evidence of bike parking, washrooms, water refill, Wi-Fi, or other cycle-specific amenities appears anywhere in the website content.
concerns: Phone number (+1 877 799 7377) is a toll-free number, likely a franchise-wide line rather than the West Kelowna location's direct contact; could not confirm on website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: An active, legitimate fast-casual dine-in and takeout cafe in West Kelowna offering substantive meals; a useful food stop for touring cyclists on the Okanagan corridor.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu page lists 'Vegetarian Breakfast Bannock' explicitly; vegan and GF options not confirmed

wow_evidence: Indigenous-owned fast-casual cafe founded by Sharon Bond-Hogg of the Nooaitch First Nation, celebrating Indigenous culinary traditions
